findings.body: Gemma 4 E2B IT (litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm) provides three published builds: GPU (2.01 GB, 2,159,332,608 bytes, LFS OID a53a59001894c58e6bdb5b9b227709f91a2e3e556baa7d85acf9c55402ba5cf5), CPU (2.59 GB, 2,776,211,200 bytes, LFS OID 181938105e0eefd105961417e8da75903eacda102c4fce9ce90f50b97139a63c), and NPU SM8750 (3.02 GB, 3,246,756,096 bytes, LFS OID 41dd675fbe735b6029012b5576a5716bac614fd8156de0128db4c9dff3cebd4e). It has a 32,768 (32k) token context window and is licensed under Apache-2.0 (open, un-gated, permits private personal applications without credentials). On Snapdragon 8 Elite (Galaxy S26 Ultra benchmark), published decode performance is 52.1 tok/s on GPU (accelerating to 91.7 tok/s with speculative decoding enabled) and 46.9 tok/s on CPU, with a 300 ms time-to-first-token (TTFT). LiteRT-LM 0.16.1 supports constrained JSON output and tool-calling on Gemma 4 via LLGuidance.

evidence.note: Primary model card documenting published binaries, 32k context, Apache-2.0 license, and Snapdragon 8 Elite benchmark numbers.
Existing ModelCatalog entries for gemma-4-E2B-it-gpu and gemma-4-E2B-it-npu-sm8750 with corresponding SHA-256 hashes.

findings.title: Gemma 4 E2B Specifications, Backends, and Snapdragon 8 Elite Benchmarks

findings.body: Gemma 4 E4B IT (litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm) provides two published builds: GPU (2.97 GB, 3,184,818,432 bytes, LFS OID 4912bb5a9c30993c51a7711f763212077458529312175df0573a78323a2bb7ff) and CPU (3.66 GB, 3,934,166,272 bytes, LFS OID 0b2a8980ce155fd97673d8e820b4d29d9c7d99b8fa6806f425d969b145bd52e0). No dedicated SM8750 NPU build is published in litert-community. It features a 32k context window and is licensed under Apache-2.0. On Snapdragon 8 Elite, published GPU decode speed is 22.1 tok/s (46.0 tok/s with speculative decoding) and CPU decode is 17.7 tok/s, with ~800 ms TTFT. It supports LiteRT-LM constrained decoding. While prose nuance is marginally higher, decode throughput is less than half that of E2B.

evidence.note: Primary model card documenting E4B files, Apache-2.0 license, and Snapdragon 8 Elite benchmarks.

findings.title: Gemma 4 E4B Specifications, Backends, and Snapdragon 8 Elite Benchmarks

findings.body: The newest small Qwen3 release in litert-community is litert-community/Qwen3-0.6B-int4. It provides two GPU/CPU builds: qwen3_0.6b_nothink_q4_block32_ekv1280.litertlm (347 MB, 364,057,088 bytes, LFS OID 2df6821ec12702dafd33915e7a1a1adc7c4b053f3672fd9555dfaf3a114c4139) and qwen3_0.6b_q4_block32_ekv1280.litertlm (347 MB, 364,057,088 bytes, LFS OID 312ce4e6bc0816edf844b9b7e66542648a89440b54822c3581e48a19e9ff5715). No dedicated NPU build exists. Context length is 1,280 tokens. License is Apache-2.0. On Snapdragon 8 Elite (SM-S937U1), published GPU performance is 69.38 tok/s decode, 1,845 tok/s prefill, 150 ms TTFT, and 585 MB peak memory. The standard build emits reasoning tags (<think>...</think>), whereas the nothink variant suppresses chain-of-thought for immediate direct answers. Larger Qwen3 small builds (1.7B and 4B) are not yet published as .litertlm in litert-community.

evidence.note: Primary model card documenting Qwen3-0.6B builds, LFS OIDs, Apache-2.0 license, and Snapdragon 8 Elite benchmarks.

findings.title: Qwen3 Small Build Specifications, Formats, and Snapdragon 8 Elite Benchmarks

findings.body: Phi-4-mini Instruct (litert-community/Phi-4-mini-instruct) publishes a single int8 multi-prefill build: Phi-4-mini-instruct_multi-prefill-seq_q8_ekv4096.litertlm (3.91 GB, 4,198,397,952 bytes, LFS OID 7764d4deb53800578307be33039476b38a6c370fff71bedb3c0552563e23ab02). It supports GPU and CPU backends (no SM8750 NPU build). Context length is 4,096 tokens. License is MIT (ungated, permits private personal apps). On Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (Galaxy S24 Ultra), published GPU decode is 10.39 tok/s, with a severe TTFT of 10.32 seconds and peak RAM consumption of 4.1 GB RSS plus 4.6 GB GPU memory (~8.7 GB total footprint). This excessive memory and latency overhead makes it unsuited for interactive on-device narration or dictation parsing.

evidence.note: Primary model card documenting file size, MIT license, 4k context, and S24 Ultra hardware metrics.

findings.body: In litert-community, SmolLM3-3B (litert-community/SmolLM3-3B) publishes SmolLM3-3B_q4_block32_ekv4096.litertlm (2.00 GB, 2,148,843,520 bytes, LFS OID 2d989ddf434a25682e580eb45dcf65c2cbd6a57f76278b8f651a8cf195c2273e) for GPU/CPU with 4,096 context and Apache-2.0 license. On Galaxy S26 (Snapdragon 8 Elite), GPU decode is 14.8 tok/s, prefill is 268 tok/s, and TTFT is 820 ms. SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct (litert-community/SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct) publishes SmolLM2-1_7B-Instruct_dynamic_wi8_afp32.litertlm (1.73 GB, 1,858,805,760 bytes, LFS OID 3c3e693157e2fb92b862b572cff74b7a353f81eb232cef682bf0fcc91855f8f1) with 8,192 context and Apache-2.0 license, but lacks published Snapdragon 8 Elite hardware benchmarks. Both underperform Gemma 4 E2B in decode throughput on the target SoC.

findings.body: Published builds for Llama 3.2 1B (1.27 GB dynamic int8) and 3B (3.24 GB dynamic int8) exist in litert-community (litert-community/Llama-3.2-1B and litert-community/Llama-3.2-3B). However, both repositories are gated under the Meta Llama 3.2 Community License, returning HTTP 401 Unauthorized for unauthenticated HTTP GET requests. LocalLLM downloads models directly on device via plain HTTPS OkHttp requests in ModelDownloadWorker without user authentication tokens (in adherence to the project security rule 'Secret and asset hygiene' in AGENTS.md). Gated models cannot be downloaded out-of-the-box by client applications, making Llama 3.2 unsuitable for LocalLLM's automated catalog promotion.

evidence.note: Primary repository showing gated status requiring Meta license agreement and auth headers.
Invariant rules requiring secret hygiene and automated unauthenticated SHA-256 download verification.

findings.title: Llama 3.2 1B and 3B Gated Repository Incompatibility with LocalLLM In-App Downloads

findings.body: Other published models under 5 GB include litert-community/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B (1.83 GB, 32k context, MIT license) and litert-community/functiongemma-270m-ft-mobile-actions (324 MB, gated under Gemma license). DeepSeek-R1 Distill is an explicit reasoning model whose mandatory chain-of-thought traces create hundreds of unnecessary reasoning tokens, introducing 5-15 seconds of unwanted latency for simple prose narration or dictation extraction. FunctionGemma is fine-tuned exclusively for mobile UI action function calling rather than general JSON classification and entity extraction, and is gated.

findings.body: LiteRT-LM 0.16.1 (com.google.ai.edge.litertlm:litertlm-android:0.16.1) integrates the LLGuidance grammar engine to support constrained decoding (strict JSON schema / grammar enforcement via enableResponseFormat) and native tool-calling via ConversationConfig.tools. This guarantees that any instruction-tuned model loaded by LiteRT-LM—including Gemma 4 E2B—can emit valid, strictly typed JSON conforming to {\"kind\":\"todo\"|\"note\",\"text\":...,\"confidence\":0..1} without parse errors or markdown formatting hallucinations.

evidence.note: Primary GitHub repository and documentation for LiteRT-LM 0.16.1 API features including constrained decoding and tool calling.

findings.title: LiteRT-LM 0.16.1 Runtime Capabilities for Constrained JSON and Tool Calling

findings.body: In app/src/main/java/com/noamv/localllm/engine/LiteRtEngine.kt, LocalLLM manages engine instances through EngineLifecycleCoordinator and a single AtomicReference<EngineHandle> (engineRef). It is architected for a single resident model instance. Loading a 2.01 GB model file from UFS 4.0 flash storage into GPU memory requires between 3,000 and 5,000 ms of initialization, shader compilation, and weight mapping. Attempting to swap models dynamically between narrating facts and voice dictation would introduce unacceptable multi-second pauses, while loading two models simultaneously would consume 2.5 to 3 GB of memory and risk GPU driver context thrashing on the Adreno 830 GPU.

evidence.note: LiteRtEngine lifecycle management confirming single resident EngineHandle reference and serialised release/load.
ADR 0001 documenting GPU runtime target and process isolation constraints.

findings.title: Single-Resident Model Architecture and Swap Latency in LocalLLM

findings.body: For Job 1 (narrating pre-computed facts into concise prose), we recommend gemma-4-E2B-it-gpu (LFS OID a53a59001894c58e6bdb5b9b227709f91a2e3e556baa7d85acf9c55402ba5cf5). With 52.1 tok/s decode (up to 91.7 tok/s with speculative decoding) and 300 ms TTFT on Snapdragon 8 Elite, it generates a 50-token narration in ~1.2 seconds. Its 2.01 GB binary leaves >10 GB of system RAM free on the 12 GB Fold 7, its Apache-2.0 license is fully ungated for public downloads, and its factual instruction-following adheres strictly to LocalLLM's SafetyPolicy.

evidence.note: Gemma 4 E2B GPU card with benchmark data and LFS OID a53a59001894c58e6bdb5b9b227709f91a2e3e556baa7d85acf9c55402ba5cf5.

findings.title: Job 1: Recommend Gemma 4 E2B GPU Build for Narrating Pre-Computed Facts

findings.body: For Job 2 (turning a dictated sentence into JSON {\"kind\":\"todo\"|\"note\",\"text\":...,\"confidence\":0..1}), we recommend gemma-4-E2B-it-gpu (LFS OID a53a59001894c58e6bdb5b9b227709f91a2e3e556baa7d85acf9c55402ba5cf5). Extracting a 25-token JSON payload takes only 300 ms TTFT + 480 ms decode (~780 ms total). Using LiteRT-LM 0.16.1's LLGuidance constrained decoding guarantees 100% schema conformity without requiring a separate specialized model.

evidence.note: Gemma 4 E2B primary card with verified throughput and LFS OID a53a59001894c58e6bdb5b9b227709f91a2e3e556baa7d85acf9c55402ba5cf5.

findings.title: Job 2: Recommend Gemma 4 E2B GPU Build with Constrained Decoding for Dictation Parsing

findings.body: We recommend keeping ONE model (Gemma 4 E2B GPU) resident in memory for both jobs rather than operating two models. Because Gemma 4 E2B is already resident for narration, executing dictation JSON extraction against it incurs 0 ms model load latency and completes in <800 ms. Swapping in a smaller model (such as Qwen3-0.6B) would introduce a 3-5 second reload delay that degrades the interactive voice dictation user experience, while concurrent dual residency creates GPU memory pressure and driver contention. A single resident general model is the optimal architectural design.

evidence.note: Single resident engine lifecycle coordinator in LiteRtEngine.
Gemma 4 E2B specifications demonstrating dual capability for text generation and structured extraction.

findings.title: Model Architecture: Recommend Keeping ONE Resident Model for Both Jobs

summary: This research evaluates candidate on-device language models for LocalLLM running on a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7 (Snapdragon 8 Elite / SM8750, 12 GB RAM) across two specific workloads: (1) narrating pre-computed facts into concise prose, and (2) transforming dictated sentences into structured JSON ({\"kind\":\"todo\"|\"note\",\"text\":...,\"confidence\":0..1}). Based on a comprehensive survey of published .litertlm models in the litert-community Hugging Face repository compatible with LiteRT-LM 0.16.1, Gemma 4 E2B remains the superior pick for Job 1 (52.1 tok/s decode, 91.7 tok/s speculative, 0.30s TTFT on Snapdragon 8 Elite, Apache 2.0 ungated license, 2.01 GB GPU binary size). For Job 2, while Qwen3-0.6B-nothink is an exceptionally fast lightweight model (347 MB, 69.4 tok/s), Gemma 4 E2B natively supports constrained JSON decoding and tool-calling via LiteRT-LM's LLGuidance engine, completing dictation JSON extraction in 600-800 ms. LocalLLM's LiteRtEngine architecture operates a single resident model instance via EngineLifecycleCoordinator; unloading Gemma 4 E2B to load a secondary model incurs a 3-5 second disk-to-GPU swap penalty that destroys voice dictation responsiveness, while dual residency risks Adreno GPU driver context contention and unnecessary RAM overhead. Therefore, keeping ONE resident model (Gemma 4 E2B GPU build, SHA-256 a53a59001894c58e6bdb5b9b227709f91a2e3e556baa7d85acf9c55402ba5cf5) for both jobs decisively outperforms deploying two models.
